summary: Builds a deduplicated vehicle-name linked list from the global vehicle array (dword_8AC390 count, dword_8AC394 base, stride 1060), clears the existing commentary list at this[4..7], then allocates one 172-byte commentary node per unique name, initializes its sub-struct arrays and text-format block, copies the name string, counts matching vehicles, sets up commentary paths via sub_414A90, and appends each node to a doubly-linked list before freeing the temporary name list.

operations.description: Iterate the vehicle array from dword_8AC394 over dword_8AC390 entries using stride 1060, reading the name byte at entry+124 for dedup collection.
Skip entries whose name byte at vehicle+124 is zero.
Compare the candidate name against each existing node's string via sub_588410, using byte_5EA438 as the null-pointer fallback string, to detect duplicates.
For a new unique name, allocate an 8-byte node via OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper and copy the name string into it with StringCopyWithBufferRealloc.
Allocate a 12-byte list node wrapping the name node, set next to null and flag byte to 1, then link it into the name list (head, tail, counter).
Traverse the existing commentary list from this[4] via the next pointer at node+4, destroying each node with MemoryAllocation_8c10(1), then zero this[4..7] (fields +0x10..+0x1C) as cleanup.

For each of the name-list entries, allocate a 172-byte commentary node and initialize its sub-struct arrays via sub_401000 with SmallEntryStructInit, plus the text-format block via TextFormatStructInitializer_4d70.
Copy the i-th name string from the temporary name list into the commentary node with StringCopyWithBufferRealloc, using byte_5EA438 as the null fallback.
Count vehicles in the array whose +124 name matches the commentary node name via sub_588410 (with NullSafePointerDereference on the node) and store the count into the node's index field.
Set up the commentary PWS/TV paths via sub_414A90 for each new node and append the node to the output list with DoublyLinkedListAppend(node, 1).
Free the temporary name list by walking the next pointers and calling DestructorWithDoubleFreePattern(1) on each node.
Return 0 to signal successful list rebuild.
